items.title: What opens first
items.body: The app opens on the My Pills tab by default. The main navigation has exactly 4 tabs: My Pills, My Habits, Events, and Settings.

items.title: What happens on launch
items.body: On the first app task, the app configures notification categories, loads Habit dashboard data, loads Pill dashboard data, loads Event dashboard data, refreshes the app badge, then runs a one-time startup health check in the background.

items.title: What happens when the app becomes active
items.body: Every time the app becomes active, both trackers run history reconciliation, refresh their dashboards, and reschedule notifications. This is the main lifecycle refresh point.

items.title: How screens open
items.body: Create screens and item Details screens for Habits, Pills, and Events open as sheets. Active Habit and Pill cards open editable Details sheets. Archive cards open the same layout in read-only mode. Restore closes the read-only Archive sheet and opens a separate editable Restore Draft sheet that finishes through the normal Save action. Event cards open editable Event Details sheets.

items.title: Device orientation
items.body: On iPhone, the app supports portrait orientation only. On iPad, the app supports portrait and landscape orientations.

items.title: Appearance modes
items.body: The app stores 3 appearance modes: System, Light, and Dark. The selected mode is applied at the app level.

items.title: App tint
items.body: Settings stores an app color: Blue, Indigo, Green, or Amber. Blue is the default app color and appears first in the palette. App colors apply to supported accent surfaces, while page backgrounds remain the system grouped background. Amber uses the iOS system orange color. Legacy stored tint values default, gray, yellow, cyan, teal, brown, red, and white are treated as Blue. Editable schedule checkmarks, Settings app-row icons, and Calendar Taken/Completed markers use the selected app color. Read-only schedule checkmarks, toggles, segmented picker selection, skipped markers, overdue and warning colors, and Backup action rows remain fixed system colors.

items.title: Badge refresh cadence
items.body: The app refreshes badge state on launch, on store changes, and with a 60-second timer while the main content is active.

items.title: Empty and loading states
items.body: If Habits are loading, the screen shows a full-screen progress indicator. If loading is complete and there are no habits, the screen shows No habits yet with the message Create your first habit to start tracking your progress.

items.title: What a Habit card shows
items.body: Each Habit card shows the name, the current schedule summary, the current streak text, the reminder text if a reminder exists, and a status icon. If there is an active overdue scheduled day, the card shows a red Today, Yesterday, or date label such as 03 May 2026. Future Habits show Starts plus the start date. Archived Habits live on the separate Archive page. Active overdue is not counted as a history gap. If recent history still needs review for another required scheduled day, the card also shows an amber warning icon. Otherwise, a green checkmark circle means completed today and a red xmark circle means skipped today.

items.title: Habit swipe actions
items.body: Leading swipe actions are used for day-state changes on active started Habits. Future and archived Habit cards do not expose day-state leading swipe actions. If today is already completed or skipped, the swipe action clears today's state with the arrow.uturn.backward system symbol. If today has no state, the swipe actions are Complete and Skip. Tapping an active Habit card opens the editable Habit Details sheet. Habit cards do not expose trailing swipe actions, and Delete is not in card swipe actions.

items.title: Habit Archive page
items.body: My Habits shows the Archive toolbar button only when at least one archived Habit exists. Archive shows archived Habits without Build or Quit sections. Archived Habit cards do not expose day-state leading swipe actions. Archived Habits open a read-only item screen with Restore and permanent Delete at the bottom.

items.title: Creating a Habit
items.body: Add new Habit includes type, name, start date, reminder toggle, reminder time, Repeat, End Repeat, and End Date. The name field uses the shared Name placeholder and word capitalization. Repeat opens a pushed editor with Days and Interval sections. Days supports weekday combinations. Interval is Every N days, limited to 2 through 5 days. Weekday summaries are Daily, Weekdays, Weekends, Weekly on Mon style labels for one selected weekday, or abbreviated day lists such as Mon, Wed, Fri for other combinations. Use schedule for history is no longer shown; new Habits use schedule-based history generation. The save button is enabled only when the habit name is not empty, the schedule rule is valid, and any selected End Date is not in the past and includes at least one scheduled day. Name, schedule, end-date, hard-limit, and unexpected action errors are shown as dismissible floating warning banners.

items.title: Habit start date range
items.body: Habit start date uses the native compact system date picker with no app-level selectable range. A future Habit remains in its normal Build or Quit dashboard section, shows Starts 03 May 2026 style dates, and has no today action/status, no overdue state, no notifications, and no history review before its start date.

items.title: Habit reminder permission behavior
items.body: If reminder is turned on during create or active Details, the app requests notification authorization. If authorization is denied, reminder is turned back off and an alert offers to open iOS Settings. iOS only shows the system notification permission prompt once, so after Don't Allow the app cannot show that prompt again.

items.title: Habit details screen
items.body: Habit Details is editable for active Habits and read-only for archived Habits. It shows name, a Streaks block with current streak, best streak, and completed for, a Schedule block with read-only Start Date, Reminder, Time when enabled, Repeat, End Repeat, and End Date when selected, plus the calendar. Active Habit Details opens the pushed Repeat editor and allows recent calendar editing. Archived Habit Details disables editing, suppresses missing-history review, and shows Restore plus permanent Delete at the bottom. The calendar shows stored history plus small tertiary system-gray dots under dates that match the effective schedule history. Active Habit Details shows a dismissible floating warning banner when any past scheduled day needs review. If the only missing day is the active overdue day, the current editable sheet asks to mark each overdue day as Completed or Skipped. Otherwise it asks to mark all past days as Completed or Skipped.

items.title: Editing a Habit
items.body: Active Habit Details saves Habit edits. It shows name, a Schedule block with read-only Start Date, Reminder, Time, Repeat, End Repeat, and End Date, an editable recent-history calendar, and Archive and Delete actions at the bottom. Start Date is informational only and is not editable after create. Repeat opens the pushed Repeat editor. Name, schedule, end-date, missing past-day, and unexpected action errors are shown as dismissible floating warning banners. Save is disabled until required history review is resolved. A past active overdue day is included in save validation and uses overdue-specific warning copy when it is the only missing day. Archive uses a system confirmation alert, Archive this Habit? / This Habit will be moved to Archive., and moves the Habit to Archive. Active Delete is permanent and uses Permanently delete this Habit? / This Habit will be permanently deleted.

items.title: How Habit history is stored
items.body: Habit history is stored in monthly HabitHistoryBucket rows plus schedule-aware HabitHistoryRange rows. Buckets hold editable and recent history. Each bucket belongs to one Habit and one local calendar month, keyed by yearMonthKey, and stores completed, skipped, and archived days as separate bit masks. Ranges hold cold generated history before the editable window without creating one database row per day. A day is completed when its bucket bit is in the positive mask or, if no bucket/legacy day exists, a valid range contains that day. A day is skipped when its bit is in the skipped mask. A day is archived when its bit is in the archived mask written by Restore for an inactive Archive gap. Restore first removes archived states on and after Active From, then writes archived bits only into empty days in the archive gap, so existing Completed or Skipped states are preserved. Archived days do not count as completed or skipped and are never editable. A day is empty only when it has no bucket bit, no valid legacy fallback row, and no valid matching range state. Legacy HabitCompletion rows are accepted only for old local data, old backups, corruption tests, and migration fallback; bucket state wins if both exist for the same day, and range state is used last.

items.title: Habit history modes
items.body: Habits store a history mode. Schedule-based means generated past history follows the selected schedule rule. Every-day means generated past history counts every day from the start date through yesterday. The selected mode is saved in the model and used later by create, details loading, backup, and restore. Dashboard cards exclude the active overdue day from history review, but active Details include a past active overdue day. Missing scheduled editable past days are not auto-filled; they block saving until the user chooses a state. The current Details screen does not show a dedicated history mode row or expose a history mode toggle.

items.title: Habit auto-fill on create
items.body: When a Habit is created, the repository generates completed history from the start date up to yesterday using schedule-based history generation. Only days matching the schedule rule are generated. Today is not prefilled. Cold generated history before the editable window is stored as a schedule-aware range, while generated days inside the editable window are stored in monthly buckets so they can still be edited individually.

items.title: Habit reconciliation
items.body: When the app becomes active or the active timer refreshes, Habits refresh derived overdue and history-review state. Reconciliation does not backfill missing Habit history and does not auto-skip overdue days. The latest due scheduled day becomes active overdue only while it is empty; older empty due scheduled days stay as history gaps until the user fixes them in active Details.

items.title: Habit editable history window
items.body: Habit Details shows the full stored calendar history. Editing is limited to the last 30 days and never goes earlier than the habit start date. Older history remains visible as historical data but is not editable.

items.title: Today versus past days in Habit edit
items.body: Today can still be empty, completed, or skipped. Every past editable scheduled Habit day must be Completed or Skipped before saving, including a past active overdue day. Saving active Habit Details does not auto-fill missing past scheduled days; if any past editable scheduled day is empty, the app shows a dismissible floating warning banner without listing dates and disables Save until the user chooses the state. If only the active overdue day is missing, the current editable sheet says Mark each overdue day as Completed or Skipped. If any other past scheduled day is missing, it says Mark all past days as Completed or Skipped. Non-scheduled editable days may still be marked manually and count when marked. If Repeat is changed, active Details creates a hidden new schedule version based on max(today, startDate), bounded by the schedule-change technical window, and normally saved at that lower bound. This hidden effectiveFrom is not shown as Apply From and is not adjusted to the next matching scheduled day.

items.title: Current streak
items.body: Current streak increases on completed days. A missing unscheduled day does not reset it. A missed scheduled day in the past resets it. Today does not reset the streak just because it is not completed yet.

items.title: Best streak and completed total
items.body: Best streak is the longest streak found by the same streak logic. Completed for is the total count of unique completed days stored in history.

items.title: Empty state
items.body: If there are no Events, the Events tab shows one empty state: No Events Yet with the message Create your first event to get started. Countdown and Count Up section headers are not shown until matching Events exist.

items.title: Event sections
items.body: The Events tab can show Countdown and Count Up sections. Countdown appears only when at least one Countdown event exists. Count Up appears only when at least one Count Up event exists.

items.title: Creating an Event
items.body: Add new Event contains a Name block and a Timing block. The name field uses the shared Name placeholder and word capitalization. Timing has Mode and Date. Mode opens a popover with Countdown and Count Up. Date uses the native compact system date picker. Countdown defaults to today. Count Up defaults to today.

items.title: Event validation
items.body: Countdown dates can be today or in the future. Past dates disable Save and show Countdown date must be in the future. Count Up dates can be today or in the past. Future dates disable Save and show Count Up date must be in the past.

items.title: Event cards
items.body: Event cards show the name on the left and duration on the right. Duration uses the same compact style as streak text, such as 2yr 2mo 7d. Duration normally uses the app tint. Countdown events show 0d in red on and after the event date. Count Up events count the selected date as day 1.

items.title: Event Details and Delete
items.body: Tapping an Event card opens Event Details. Event Details can edit name, mode, and date. Delete is permanent and uses the confirmation Delete this Event? / This Event will be permanently deleted. Events do not use Archive, Restore, reminders, overdue, badge count, history review, or auto-delete. For persistence and backup compatibility, user-facing Count Up is stored with the raw mode value elapsed.

items.title: Empty and loading states
items.body: If Pills are loading, the screen shows a full-screen progress indicator. If loading is complete and there are no pills, the screen shows No pills yet with the message Create your first pill to track dosage, reminders, and taken days.

items.title: How Pill cards are grouped
items.body: The Pill dashboard is split into exactly 2 sections: Today and Pending. Today contains pills scheduled for today. Pending contains the rest.

items.title: What a Pill card shows
items.body: Each Pill card shows the name, dosage, schedule summary, total taken days, reminder text if a reminder exists, and a status icon. If there is an active overdue scheduled day, the card shows a red Today, Yesterday, or date label such as 03 May 2026. Future Pills appear in Pending and show Starts plus the start date. Archived Pills live on the separate Archive page. Active overdue is not counted as a history gap. If recent history still needs review for another required scheduled day, the card also shows an amber warning icon. Otherwise, a green checkmark circle means taken today and a red xmark circle means skipped today.

items.title: Pill swipe actions
items.body: Leading swipe actions are used for day-state changes on active started Pills. Future and archived Pill cards do not expose day-state leading swipe actions. If today is already taken or skipped, the swipe action clears today's state with the arrow.uturn.backward system symbol. If today has no state, the swipe actions are Taken and Skip. Tapping an active Pill card opens the editable Pill Details sheet. Pill cards do not expose trailing swipe actions, and Delete is not in card swipe actions.

items.title: Pill Archive page
items.body: My Pills shows the Archive toolbar button only when at least one archived Pill exists. Archive shows archived Pills without Today or Pending sections. Archived Pill cards do not expose day-state leading swipe actions. Archived Pills open a read-only item screen with Restore and permanent Delete at the bottom.

items.title: Creating a Pill
items.body: Add new Pill includes name, dosage, start date, reminder toggle, reminder time, Repeat, End Repeat, End Date, and an optional description. The name field uses the shared Name placeholder and word capitalization. The optional description field uses the Add notes… placeholder. Repeat opens a pushed editor with Days and Interval sections. Days supports weekday combinations. Interval includes Never for one-time Pills and Every N days, limited to 2 through 5 days. Weekday summaries are Daily, Weekdays, Weekends, Weekly on Mon style labels for one selected weekday, or abbreviated day lists such as Mon, Wed, Fri for other combinations. Use schedule for history is no longer shown; new Pills use schedule-based history generation. Save is enabled only when the pill name is not empty, the dosage is not empty, the schedule rule is valid, and any selected End Date is not in the past and includes at least one scheduled day. Name, dosage, schedule, end-date, hard-limit, and unexpected action errors are shown as dismissible floating warning banners.

items.title: Pill start date range
items.body: Pill start date uses the native compact system date picker with no app-level selectable range. A future Pill appears in Pending and shows Starts 03 May 2026 style dates, but it has no today action/status, no overdue state, no notifications, and no history review before its start date.

items.title: Pill details screen
items.body: Pill Details is editable for active Pills and read-only for archived Pills. It shows name, dosage, a Streak block with Taken for, a Schedule block with read-only Start Date, Reminder, Time when enabled, Repeat, End Repeat, and End Date when selected, plus the calendar and optional description. Active Pill Details opens the pushed Repeat editor and allows recent calendar editing. Archived Pill Details disables editing, suppresses missing-history review, and shows Restore plus permanent Delete at the bottom. The calendar shows stored history plus small tertiary system-gray dots under dates that match the effective schedule history. Active Pill Details shows a dismissible floating warning banner when any past scheduled day needs review. If the only missing day is the active overdue day, the current editable sheet asks to mark each overdue day as Taken or Skipped. Otherwise it asks to mark all past days as Taken or Skipped.

items.title: Editing a Pill
items.body: Active Pill Details saves Pill edits. It shows name, dosage, a Schedule block with read-only Start Date, Reminder, Time, Repeat, End Repeat, and End Date, an editable recent-history calendar, description, and Archive and Delete actions at the bottom. Start Date is informational only and is not editable after create. Repeat opens the pushed Repeat editor. Name, dosage, schedule, end-date, missing past-day, and unexpected action errors are shown as dismissible floating warning banners. Save is disabled until required history review is resolved. A past active overdue day is included in save validation and uses overdue-specific warning copy when it is the only missing day. Archive uses a system confirmation alert, Archive this Pill? / This Pill will be moved to Archive., and moves the Pill to Archive. Active Delete is permanent and uses Permanently delete this Pill? / This Pill will be permanently deleted.

items.title: How Pill history is stored
items.body: Pill history is stored in monthly PillHistoryBucket rows plus schedule-aware PillHistoryRange rows. Buckets hold editable and recent history. Each bucket belongs to one Pill and one local calendar month, keyed by yearMonthKey, and stores taken, skipped, and archived days as separate bit masks. Ranges hold cold generated history before the editable window without creating one database row per day. A day is taken when its bucket bit is in the positive mask or, if no bucket/legacy day exists, a valid range contains that day. A day is skipped when its bit is in the skipped mask. A day is archived when its bit is in the archived mask written by Restore for an inactive Archive gap. Restore first removes archived states on and after Active From, then writes archived bits only into empty days in the archive gap, so existing Taken or Skipped states are preserved. Archived days do not count as taken or skipped and are never editable. A day is empty only when it has no bucket bit, no valid legacy fallback row, and no valid matching range state. Legacy PillIntake rows are accepted only for old local data, old backups, corruption tests, and migration fallback; bucket state wins if both exist for the same day, and range state is used last.

items.title: Pill history modes
items.body: Pills store a history mode. Schedule-based means generated past history follows the selected schedule rule. Every-day means generated past history counts every day from the start date through yesterday. The selected mode is saved and used later by create, details loading, backup, and restore. Dashboard cards exclude the active overdue day from history review, but active Details include a past active overdue day. Missing scheduled editable past days are not auto-filled; they block saving until the user chooses a state. The current Details screen does not show a dedicated history mode row or expose a history mode toggle.

items.title: Pill prefilled taken history on create
items.body: When a new Pill is created, the repository generates taken history from the start date up to yesterday using schedule-based history generation. Only days matching the schedule rule are generated. Cold generated history before the editable window is stored as a schedule-aware range, while generated days inside the editable window are stored in monthly buckets so they can still be edited individually.

items.title: What repository create does for Pills
items.body: When the Pill is saved, the repository writes generated taken history from startDate through yesterday. Cold generated history before the editable window is stored as one schedule-aware PillHistoryRange, while generated days inside the editable window are stored in monthly PillHistoryBucket rows. Today is not prefilled.

items.title: Pill reconciliation
items.body: When the app becomes active or the active timer refreshes, Pills refresh derived overdue and history-review state. Reconciliation does not backfill missing Pill history and does not auto-skip overdue days. The latest due scheduled day becomes active overdue only while it is empty; older empty due scheduled days stay as history gaps until the user fixes them in active Details.

items.title: Pill editable history window
items.body: Pill Details shows the full stored calendar history. Editing is limited to the last 30 days and never goes earlier than the pill start date. Older history remains visible as historical data but is not editable.

items.title: Today versus past days in Pill edit
items.body: Today can still be empty, taken, or skipped. Every past editable scheduled Pill day must be Taken or Skipped before saving, including a past active overdue day. Saving active Pill Details does not auto-fill missing past scheduled days; if any past editable scheduled day is empty, the app shows a dismissible floating warning banner without listing dates and disables Save until the user chooses the state. If only the active overdue day is missing, the current editable sheet says Mark each overdue day as Taken or Skipped. If any other past scheduled day is missing, it says Mark all past days as Taken or Skipped. Non-scheduled editable days may still be marked manually and count when marked. If Repeat is changed, active Details creates a hidden new schedule version based on max(today, startDate), bounded by the schedule-change technical window, and normally saved at that lower bound. This hidden effectiveFrom is not shown as Apply From and is not adjusted to the next matching scheduled day.

items.title: Pill totals
items.body: Pills do not use streaks. Taken for is the total count of unique taken days stored in history.

items.title: Notification categories
items.body: Habits use actions Mark as Completed and Mark as Skipped. Pills use Mark as Taken, Mark as Skipped, and Remind me in 10 mins.

items.title: Scheduling window
items.body: The app schedules reminder notifications only for the next 2 days. It does not build an unlimited long-range pending queue.

items.title: Grouped reminders
items.body: If fewer than 3 reminders land on the same scheduled time, the app creates individual reminders. If 3 or more reminders land on the same scheduled time, the app creates a single aggregated reminder for that time.

items.title: When reminders are eligible
items.body: A reminder candidate is created only when reminder is enabled, the item is not archived, the local day is not before the item start date, the local day is not after the final scheduled day when End Date exists, the local day matches the current schedule rule, the day is not already completed or taken, the day is not already skipped, and the scheduled reminder time is still in the future. Reminder planning intentionally scans the next 2 local days; this is currently accepted for sparse weekly and interval schedules because the expected usage pattern is daily app opens, which trigger a fresh reschedule.

items.title: What tapping a reminder does
items.body: Default tapping an individual or aggregated Habit reminder opens My Habits. Default tapping an individual or aggregated Pill reminder opens My Pills.

items.title: How day resolution works
items.body: Reminder actions do not trust the delivery timestamp as the only source of truth. They use localDate from the notification payload first, and only fall back to the notification date if localDate is missing or invalid.

items.title: Pill remind later
items.body: Remind me in 10 mins creates a separate delayed Pill reminder using minute-level calendar precision. Because seconds are intentionally not preserved, the delayed reminder may fire up to 59 seconds earlier than an exact second-level 10-minute delay; this is accepted by customer requirements. The delayed reminder keeps the original pillID and localDate in its payload.

items.title: Pill remind later persistence
items.body: Snoozed Pill reminders are kept separate from regular scheduled reminders. A global Pill reschedule removes only regular Pill reminders and leaves active remind-later reminders in place. Snoozed reminders are removed when the same pill and day are taken or skipped, or when the pill is deleted.

items.title: What the badge counts
items.body: The app badge is the total number of overdue Habits plus overdue Pills.

items.title: When a Habit is overdue
items.body: A Habit is overdue when it is not archived and the latest due scheduled day is empty. Scheduled days become due at reminder time, or at 00:00 when reminders are disabled. Older empty due scheduled days are history gaps, not active overdue.

items.title: When a Pill is overdue
items.body: A Pill is overdue when it is not archived and the latest due scheduled day is empty. Scheduled days become due at reminder time, or at 00:00 when reminders are disabled. Older empty due scheduled days are history gaps, not active overdue.

items.title: Projected badge count in notifications
items.body: When the app builds reminder notifications, it also calculates a projected overdue badge count for the exact scheduled reminder time of each notification request.

items.title: What overdue does not do
items.body: Badge calculation is derived state only. Reconciliation does not persist skipped states for overdue catch-up.

items.title: What overdue does not change
items.body: When a newer scheduled due day appears, older empty due scheduled days become history gaps. They remain manual review and can only be fixed in Edit.

items.title: End Repeat, End Date, Archive, and Restore
items.body: End Repeat is optional for both Pills and Habits. The Schedule UI shows an End Repeat options row with Never or On Date; the End Date picker row appears only for On Date. If a date is selected, the final active scheduled day is the last scheduled day on or before that date. The End Date row uses the native compact system date picker with no app-level selectable range. A selected End Date is valid only when it is not in the past and at least one scheduled day exists between the active lower bound and the selected date. If the selected date is before local today, Save stays disabled and the app shows the dismissible floating warning End date can’t be in the past. If the selected date is today or later but the range contains no scheduled day, the warning says End date must include at least one scheduled day. Save does not silently raise End Date. Once the final day is taken/completed or skipped, the item moves to Archive automatically without confirmation. If the final day remains empty, the item stays active and can become overdue. Manual Archive uses confirmation and preserves reminder, repeat, end date, and history as historical data. Manual and automatic Archive store archivedAt as the actual local day the Archive operation runs. Archived items can be restored through Restore Draft. Saving a valid Restore Draft asks whether to Keep History or Start Fresh. Keep History starts a new active cycle from Active From and stores Archive gap days with the archived source only when those days are empty. Start Fresh clears old history, sets Start Date to Active From, and returns the item with empty calendar history and reset streak/count totals. Repeat Never for Pills is a one-time schedule on Start Date, clears and ignores End Date, and moves the Pill to Archive automatically after that day is taken or skipped.

items.title: What Backup screen shows
items.body: Settings shows Backup with the subtitle Manual and automatic backups. Backup shows Last backup, Total size, Folder, and Auto Backup. Last backup uses the same color as its cloud status icon, green when a readable backup exists and red when it does not, and dates use 03 May at 22:35 style formatting. Auto Backup is a user-controlled toggle with the clock.arrow.trianglehead.clockwise.rotate.90.path.dotted icon, but the app can turn it off for safety when the selected destination is not trusted. Create Backup and Restore Backup are full-width capsule buttons; Create uses the primary label color and Restore stays system red. Create and Restore confirmations use system alerts instead of popover confirmation dialogs; alert actions use short labels: Backup and Restore. Backup feedback uses dismissible floating banners that auto-hide after 4 seconds or clear when leaving the Backup screen. The Home Screen app icon exposes a Create Backup quick action; choosing it opens Settings > Backup only, and backup creation still starts only after the user taps Create Backup on the Backup screen.

items.title: Auto Backup
items.body: Auto Backup reuses the normal backup writer, file names, schema, rotation, and selected folder. Auto Backup can be On only when the selected destination is trusted: the folder is usable and either has no backup file yet, has a backup last created by this app install, or has a backup last restored by this app install. If Auto Backup is turned on with no folder selected, the folder picker opens; choosing an empty or trusted folder enables Auto Backup, while cancelling keeps it off. If the selected folder contains a readable backup that has not been restored, or an unreadable backup, Auto Backup stays Off and shows Create or restore a backup before turning on Auto Backup. If destination trust is later lost, Auto Backup turns Off during screen load, startup, foreground, background, or the next automatic backup attempt. Auto Backup runs only when it is On, data is dirty, the selected destination is trusted, and no backup or restore operation is already running. Data changes wait 20 seconds before an automatic backup; another change resets the timer. Startup, foreground, and background also check for pending dirty data. Automatic backup failures stay silent outside the Backup screen and keep dirty data pending for a later retry.

items.title: Folder with an existing backup
items.body: Choosing a folder never restores data automatically. Backup action notices are derived from the selected folder state and remembered backup fingerprints, not from a temporary screen session. If the folder contains a readable backup that has not been created or restored by this app install, the Backup screen shows Backup available. Restore when ready. as a blue floating informational banner and disables Create Backup. If the same backup was already created or restored by this app install, no restore-needed informational banner is shown.

items.title: Folder without a backup
items.body: If the selected folder has no readable backup, Backup shows No backup found. Create one to get started. as a blue floating informational banner. Create Backup stays available and Restore Backup is disabled.

items.title: Unreadable backup files
items.body: If backup files exist but cannot be read, Backup shows Backup can’t be read. Choose another location or create a new one. as a red floating banner. Restore Backup is disabled. Backup Created and Restore Complete are green floating success banners.

items.title: Backup file names
items.body: The main backup file is LoonyBear.json.gz. If a previous main backup exists, it is moved to LoonyBear.previous.json.gz before a new main backup is written.

items.title: What backup includes
items.body: Backup includes Habits, Habit schedule rules, Habit monthly history buckets, Habit schedule-aware history ranges, legacy Habit completions for old backup compatibility, Habit ordering, Pills, Pill schedule rules, Pill monthly history buckets, Pill schedule-aware history ranges, legacy Pill intakes for old backup compatibility, reminder settings, stored history modes, optional End Date values, stored Archive/isArchived state, archivedAt dates, archived history sources, Events, and app appearance settings.

items.title: Restore safety snapshot
items.body: Before restore, the app tries to create a restore snapshot file named LoonyBear.restore-snapshot.json.gz. If snapshot payload creation fails because the local store is already corrupted, restore can still continue. If snapshot encoding, compression, or writing fails, restore is aborted.

items.title: Restore validation
items.body: Restore validates schema version, app appearance settings when present, history mode values, schedule rules including interval and one-time kinds, source values, monthly bucket masks and counts, schedule-aware range owner IDs, date order, counts, schedule payloads, and duplicate identifiers before replacing the store.

items.title: What restore does after success
items.body: After a successful restore, the app resets the read context, applies backed-up theme mode and app tint when present, refreshes dashboards, and rebuilds Habit and Pill notifications from restored data. Legacy backups without app settings keep the current theme and tint.

items.title: Folder access
items.body: Backup uses a stored security-scoped folder bookmark. If the bookmark is no longer valid, the Backup screen asks the user to choose the folder again before backup or restore can continue.

items.title: Settings sections
items.body: Settings contains an Appearance card with System, Light, and Dark mode plus the app color palette; an App card with Backup and Rules & Logic; and an About card. About shows the current app version and build.

items.title: What Rules & Logic is
items.body: Rules & Logic is a local reference screen loaded from RulesLogicContent.json inside the app bundle. If the file cannot be loaded or decoded, the screen shows Rules & Logic unavailable.

items.title: Version footer
items.body: Settings shows Version <short version> and Build <build number> from the app bundle metadata. Build numbers are auto-incremented from CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION during normal builds and displayed as a six-digit value, for example 001025. Xcode previews skip the increment. Because CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION lives in the Xcode project, a normal build can leave project.pbxproj changed by the build-number bump.

items.title: Top-level composition
items.body: The app is composed from LoonyBearApp, AppEnvironment, ContentView, and RootTabView. AppEnvironment builds HabitAppState, PillAppState, NotificationService, PillNotificationService, AppBadgeService, AppNotificationCoordinator, and WidgetSyncService dependencies.

items.title: Main state holders
items.body: HabitAppState owns Habit dashboard loading, create, update, delete, daily mutations, detail state loading, reconciliation trigger, and Habit notification preparation. PillAppState owns the same responsibilities for Pills, plus Pill reordering.

items.title: Storage architecture
items.body: All persisted application data is stored in Core Data. Habits and Pills use separate repositories: CoreDataHabitRepository and CoreDataPillRepository. Both repositories use a shared CoreDataRepositoryContext for background writes and read-context refresh.

items.title: Screen model
items.body: The app uses a tab root with sheet-based create and item Details flows. The default tab is My Pills. Sheets are identified by enum state carrying either a fixed mode or a UUID. Active item sheets are editable Details screens; archived item sheets use the same layout in read-only mode and can enter Restore Draft. Restore Draft saves through a system confirmation choice: Keep History keeps prior history, while Start Fresh clears prior history and uses Active From as the new Start Date.

items.title: Calendar navigation
items.body: Shared month calendars use header chevron buttons for month navigation. Horizontal swipe paging is disabled on Details calendar surfaces. Calendar blocks keep a stable six-week footprint and adjust vertical row spacing for shorter months. Habit and Pill Details calendar day views show a small tertiary system-gray dot under dates that match the effective schedule history. Archived rows show as quiet system-gray circles that ignore the app tint. Active Details calendars show full stored history but only allow taps inside the editable 30-day window, never before Start Date, and never on archived rows. Archive read-only calendars are not editable. Restore Draft calendars become editable from Active From inside the normal editable window; archived gap rows before Active From stay read-only.

items.title: Repeat editor
items.body: Create and active Details screens open Repeat as a pushed screen inside the current sheet. The screen has Days and Interval sections. Days shows full weekday names with checkmarks and prevents leaving the schedule empty. Interval uses Every N days [Stepper] with a native Stepper, limited to 2 through 5 days, and for Pills only also includes Never. Archive read-only Details show Repeat as text and do not open a schedule picker until the user enters Restore Draft.

items.title: Settings navigation persistence
items.body: Settings uses route-based navigation for Backup and Rules & Logic. Settings child screens keep the custom tinted back button and preserve the native left-edge swipe-back gesture. The selected tab and active Settings route are stored in scene storage so restore-driven appearance changes and tint rebuilds do not drop the user out of the Backup screen.

items.title: Habit model types
items.body: HabitType has exactly 2 values: build and quit. CompletionSource has exactly 7 values: swipe, manual edit, notification, restore, auto fill, skipped, and archived. HabitHistoryMode has exactly 2 values: scheduleBased and everyDay.

items.title: Pill model types
items.body: PillCompletionSource has exactly 6 values: swipe, manual edit, notification, restore, skipped, and archived. PillHistoryMode has exactly 2 values: scheduleBased and everyDay.

items.title: Reminder time rules
items.body: ReminderTime stores hour and minute as integers. ReminderTime.default rounds the current time up to a 5-minute boundary. If rounding reaches 60 minutes, the hour is incremented and minute becomes 0. Create and active Details reminder time rows use the native compact system time picker. Create Start Date rows use the native compact system date picker with no app-level selectable range; active Details show Start Date as read-only. End Date rows use the native compact system date picker with no app-level selectable range and use shared schedule-aware validation instead of silent Save correction. Schedule blocks keep native system pickers and protect them with a shared presentation guard: while the End Repeat options popover is open, neighboring compact pickers ignore hit-testing; Time and End Repeat touch-downs briefly block the opposite presentation path through a non-cancelling window-level observer; and Repeat navigation dismisses and briefly blocks End Repeat so the popover cannot survive over the pushed Repeat screen.

items.title: Schedule model
items.body: ScheduleRule stores weekday selections as weekly WeekdaySet bitmasks, Every N days as intervalDays, or Never repeat as a one-time Pill rule. Weekday summaries are labels derived from the selected days: Daily for Monday through Sunday, Weekdays for Monday through Friday, Weekends for Saturday and Sunday, Weekly on Mon style labels for one selected weekday, and abbreviated day lists such as Mon, Wed, Fri for other weekday combinations. IntervalDays is limited to 2 through 5 days. Initial interval schedules are anchored to the item start date; edited interval schedules are anchored to the active schedule version effectiveFrom. Legacy daily, weekdays, and weekends schedule kind values are read back as weekly masks.

items.title: Persistence container
items.body: The persistent container name is LoonyBear. Persistent store descriptions enable automatic lightweight migration and inferred mapping models so additive model changes can migrate existing local stores. The main viewContext automatically merges parent changes and uses NSMergeByPropertyObjectTrumpMergePolicy. Background contexts use the same merge policy.

items.title: Read and write coordination
items.body: Repositories perform writes through CoreDataRepositoryContext.performWrite. After a successful write, the read context is refreshed with refreshAllObjects. If the read context is main queue and the current thread is already main, refreshAllObjects is called directly.

items.title: Editable history window
items.body: EditableHistoryWindow.dates returns up to 30 days ending at today, never earlier than startDate. EditableHistoryWindow.pastDates returns the same window without today.

items.title: Past day normalization
items.body: EditableHistoryContract.normalizedSelection normalizes all day sets to start-of-day values and fills missing required past days using either positive or skipped default selection. Any skipped day that is also positive is removed from the skipped set.

items.title: Schedule applicability
items.body: HistoryScheduleApplicability can compute past editable days, past scheduled editable days, past required editable days, and scheduled calendar indicator days. Effective schedule for a given day is the latest schedule version whose effectiveFrom is not later than that day, ordered by effectiveFrom, version, and createdAt. Weekly rules use weekday membership. Every-N-days interval rules use the active schedule version effectiveFrom as the interval anchor. Create stores the first schedule version at Start Date. Active Details stores a new schedule version only when Repeat changes. Apply From is not exposed in the UI; the hidden schedule-change effectiveFrom is based on max(today, startDate), bounded by the end of the second next calendar month, and normally saved at the lower bound. The resolver does not move it to the next matching weekday or skip explicit history states. The calendar preview drops replaced future schedule versions so dots match the post-save schedule.

items.title: Create Habit validations
items.body: CreateHabitUseCase requires a non-empty trimmed name and a valid schedule rule. CoreDataHabitRepository also enforces a hard limit of 20 habits. Create Habit also validates optional End Date before Save: the selected date must not be in the past and must include at least one scheduled day from the active lower bound through End Date. Create Habit presents form validation, hard-limit errors, end-date errors, and unexpected action failures with the shared dismissible floating warning banner.

items.title: Habit create storage
items.body: Habit creation inserts a Habit row, inserts the first HabitScheduleVersion row, stores schedule-based historyModeRaw, stores optional End Date, sets isArchived to false, clears archivedAt, and writes generated initial completed history from startDate through yesterday by splitting it into one cold schedule-aware HabitHistoryRange before the editable window plus monthly HabitHistoryBucket rows inside the editable window.

items.title: Habit create autofill source
items.body: Habit create history generation writes completed facts. Only days matching the schedule rule are generated. Today is not prefilled. Cold generated history stores its schedule payload and count in a range row; editable generated history stores completed bucket bits. Bucketed positive history stores the completed fact, not the old day-level source provenance; projected domain completions use the manual-edit compatibility source.

items.title: Habit update behavior
items.body: Habit update changes name, reminder fields, optional End Date, and optionally inserts a new HabitScheduleVersion if the schedule rule changed. Apply From is hidden; the new schedule version starts at the hidden effectiveFrom based on max(today, startDate), bounded by the end of the second next calendar month, and normally saved at the lower bound. This hidden resolver is schedule-agnostic and does not skip explicit history states. Editable history is normalized and written back day by day using manual edit or skipped sources. Update validation requires every past editable scheduled day to be Completed or Skipped; missing scheduled past states block save instead of being auto-filled. Archived Habits open read-only Details; Restore Draft is the only path that edits and unarchives an archived Habit.

items.title: Habit today actions
items.body: completeHabitToday writes a completed state or converts an existing skipped state to completed. skipHabitToday writes skipped if no state exists and leaves already skipped states unchanged. clearHabitDayStateToday clears today's state if it exists. When a card has an active overdue day, card swipe actions apply to that overdue day instead of today.

items.title: Habit reconciliation behavior
items.body: Habit reconciliation is a no-op for stored history state. It does not auto-fill missing past Habit history and does not auto-skip older overdue days. Dashboard and badge state are derived from the latest due scheduled day, while older missing scheduled days stay in manual review.

items.title: Create Pill validations
items.body: Create Pill requires a non-empty trimmed name, a non-empty trimmed dosage, and a valid schedule rule. CoreDataPillRepository also enforces a hard limit of 20 pills. Create Pill also validates optional End Date before Save unless Repeat is Never: the selected date must not be in the past and must include at least one scheduled day from the active lower bound through End Date. Repeat Never clears and ignores End Date. Create Pill presents form validation, hard-limit errors, end-date errors, and unexpected action failures with the shared dismissible floating warning banner.

items.title: Create Pill day generation
items.body: During repository create, initial taken history is generated from startDate through yesterday. Generation includes only days matching the schedule rule. Today is not prefilled. Cold generated history before the editable window is written as one schedule-aware PillHistoryRange, while editable-window generated history is written into monthly PillHistoryBucket rows.

items.title: Pill create storage
items.body: Pill creation inserts a Pill row, inserts the first PillScheduleVersion row, stores schedule-based historyModeRaw, stores optional End Date, sets isArchived to false, clears archivedAt, and writes generated taken history from startDate through yesterday by splitting it into one cold schedule-aware PillHistoryRange before the editable window plus monthly PillHistoryBucket rows inside the editable window. Today is not prefilled. Bucketed positive history stores the taken fact, not separate day-level source provenance; projected domain intakes use the manual-edit compatibility source.

items.title: Pill update behavior
items.body: Pill update changes name, dosage, details, reminder fields, optional End Date, and optionally inserts a new PillScheduleVersion if the schedule rule changed. Apply From is hidden; the new schedule version starts at the hidden effectiveFrom based on max(today, startDate), bounded by the end of the second next calendar month, and normally saved at the lower bound. This hidden resolver is schedule-agnostic and does not skip explicit history states. Repeat Never clears and ignores End Date. Editable history is normalized and written back day by day using manual edit or skipped sources. Update validation requires every past editable scheduled day to be Taken or Skipped; missing scheduled past states block save instead of being auto-filled. Archived Pills open read-only Details; Restore Draft is the only path that edits and unarchives an archived Pill.

items.title: Pill today actions
items.body: markTakenToday writes a taken state or converts an existing skipped state to taken. skipPillToday writes skipped if no state exists and leaves already skipped states unchanged. clearPillDayStateToday clears today's state if it exists. When a card has an active overdue day, card swipe actions apply to that overdue day instead of today.

items.title: Pill reconciliation behavior
items.body: Pill reconciliation is a no-op for stored history state. It does not backfill missing past Pill history and does not auto-skip older overdue days. Dashboard and badge state are derived from the latest due scheduled day, while older missing scheduled days stay in manual review.

items.title: Shared notification helpers
items.body: NotificationSupport defines Notification.Name keys for store changes and tab opening, a NotificationStoreContext for Core Data notification reads and writes, local notification authorization helpers, stale delivered cleanup, pending request removal helpers, and localDate identifier encoding and parsing.

items.title: Habit notification constants
items.body: Habit notifications use categoryIdentifier habit.reminder, summaryCategoryIdentifier habit.reminder.summary, action identifiers habit.complete and habit.skip, schedulingWindowDays 2, and aggregationThreshold 3. The 2-day planning window is accepted for now for both weekly and interval schedules because lifecycle refreshes are expected daily.

items.title: Pill notification constants
items.body: Pill notifications use categoryIdentifier pill.reminder, summaryCategoryIdentifier pill.reminder.summary, action identifiers pill.take, pill.skip, and pill.remind_later, schedulingWindowDays 2, aggregationThreshold 3, and remindLaterInterval 600 seconds with accepted minute-level trigger precision. The 2-day planning window is accepted for now for both weekly and interval schedules because lifecycle refreshes are expected daily.

items.title: Reminder candidate rules
items.body: Both Habit and Pill reminder services build candidates only when reminder is enabled, reminderTime exists, the item is not archived, the local day is not before startDate, the local day is not before activeFrom when a restored cycle has a later activeFrom, the local day is not after the final scheduled day when End Date exists, the local day matches the active schedule rule, the local day is not already completed or taken, the local day is not skipped, and the scheduled reminder time is still in the future.

items.title: Default tap routing
items.body: Habit default taps route aggregated and individual Habit notifications to My Habits. Pill default taps route pill_aggregated and pill notifications to My Pills.

items.title: Badge calculation
items.body: AppBadgeService calculates overdue Habits and overdue Pills separately and sums them. Overdue means activeOverdueDay is set from the latest due scheduled day while that day is empty. Older history gaps are not badge-counted overdue. Dashboard cards do not count active overdue as a history review gap while it remains actionable; active Details still surface a past active overdue day as requiring review.

items.title: Backup schema and files
items.body: Backup schemaVersion is 3. The main backup file is LoonyBear.json.gz. The previous backup file is LoonyBear.previous.json.gz. The restore snapshot file is LoonyBear.restore-snapshot.json.gz. Current backups store Habit and Pill history as monthly bucket payloads plus schedule-aware range payloads. Auto Backup does not add a new file name, schema, Core Data entity, or archive format; it writes the same backup as manual Create Backup. New builds can restore older v1 backups that do not contain bucket history, range history, scheduleKind, intervalDays, End Date, Archive/isArchived state, archivedAt, archived history sources, Events, or app settings; old day-level history payloads are restored into buckets. Legacy v2 backups without range payloads remain valid and default missing range arrays to empty. Restoring new backups into older app builds is not supported.

items.title: Backup payload contents
items.body: BackupArchive contains habits with End Date, Archive/isArchived state, archivedAt, habit schedule versions with schedule kind, weekday mask, and interval days, habit monthly history buckets including archived masks, habit schedule-aware history ranges, habit ordering, optional app settings, pills with End Date, Archive/isArchived state, archivedAt, pill schedule versions with schedule kind, weekday mask, and interval days, pill monthly history buckets including archived masks, pill schedule-aware history ranges, and Events. Schedule kind can represent weekly, custom interval days, or one-time Pill rules. BackupHabit and BackupPill both carry stored historyMode values. BackupEvent carries name, mode, date, sort order, timestamps, and version. BackupAppSettings carries appearanceMode and appTint.

items.title: Backup file state
items.body: BackupStatus includes a fileState: none, available, created, restored, or unreadable. Readable backup files are fingerprinted from their compressed data using SHA-256. Successful create stores the last created fingerprint; successful restore stores the last restored fingerprint. BackupStatus.allowsAutomaticBackup is true only when the folder is usable and fileState is none, created, or restored. It is false for available and unreadable, so Auto Backup cannot overwrite a readable backup that the user has not restored and cannot write over corrupt backup data.

items.title: Auto Backup service
items.body: AutoBackupService stores backup_auto_enabled, backup_auto_dirty, and backup_auto_dirty_generation in UserDefaults. AppStateWriteCoordinator marks dirty after successful UI writes, notification action mutations are covered through habit, pill, and event store-change notifications, and backed-up Settings changes mark dirty directly. Dirty state survives app restart. Successful manual or automatic backup clears dirty only when no newer change happened while that backup was running. Successful manual restore clears dirty and does not schedule an immediate automatic backup of the restored store; the restored backup becomes the baseline until the next real mutation. BackupService serializes create and restore with an operation lock, so manual backup, automatic backup, and restore do not write files in parallel.

items.title: Restore safety and validation
items.body: Restore first attempts to create a compressed snapshot of the current store. If snapshot payload creation fails with a DataIntegrityError, restore continues. If snapshot encoding, compression, or file writing fails, restore aborts. Restore validates schema version, app settings when present, history modes, reminder times, schedule rules including interval and one-time kinds, source values, monthly bucket masks and counts, history range owner IDs, date order, counts, schedule payloads, foreign key references, and duplicate identifiers before replacing the store.

items.title: Reliability layer
items.body: ReliabilitySupport defines DataIntegrityIssue, DataIntegrityReport, DataIntegrityError, IntegrityReportBuilder, ReminderValidation, WeekdayValidation, and ReliabilityLog. DataIntegrityError reports the operation name and the count of corrupted records detected.

items.title: Compression service
items.body: CompressionService performs gzip compression and decompression using zlib. The two failure cases exposed by the service are compressionFailed and decompressionFailed.

items.title: Widget snapshot system
items.body: WidgetSyncService writes a WidgetSnapshot built from the Habit dashboard only. It skips unchanged content, writes on a utility queue, retries the same content if a previous save failed, and reloads all widget timelines only after a successful changed save. WidgetSnapshotStore saves into app group group.com.valr4k.LoonyBear when available, otherwise into Application Support under LoonyBear/widget-snapshot.json.
